subject.title: Prompt-cache prefix churn on OpenAI models: per-turn dynamic injections (message tool hint + volatile system-prompt section) defeat automatic prefix caching

question: Should OpenClaw prioritize byte-stable OpenAI/Codex cached prefixes by moving `message_tool_only` reply-delivery guidance out of tool schemas and system-prompt prefix content, or keep the current delivery-first prompt placement despite cache churn?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug crosses prompt-cache economics, Codex/OpenAI request shape, and source-channel visible reply semantics; automation should not choose the permanent delivery-guidance boundary without maintainer intent and live proof expectations.

options.title: Move guidance to late turn content
options.body: Recommended: keep tool schemas and system-prompt prefix stable, inject the per-turn visible-reply directive into late current-turn content, and prove both visible delivery and OpenAI cache reuse.

options.title: Preserve current prompt placement
options.body: Accept the cache churn as the cost of stronger per-turn delivery steering and document the OpenAI/Codex prompt-cache limitation for message-heavy orchestrator sessions.

options.title: Defer to broader cache redesign
options.body: Keep this issue open as part of a broader prompt-cache architecture pass spanning active-memory, current-time, and pruning, delaying a narrow fix for the pinned `message_tool_only` churn.

recommendation.title: Move guidance to late turn content
recommendation.body: Recommended: keep tool schemas and system-prompt prefix stable, inject the per-turn visible-reply directive into late current-turn content, and prove both visible delivery and OpenAI cache reuse.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits on system-prompt delivery guidance make this the best available owner for deciding where the per-turn delivery contract should live.
